A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GyroSwin study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original GKW simulations and trained-surrogate evaluations, including ID/OOD rollout and heat-flux results, physical diagnostics and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original simulation and surrogate-evaluation results and adds model/data scaling experiments and fitted scaling relationships in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix D changes the reported training procedure substantially. v3 ramps heat-flux supervision into joint training, ending with all three loss weights equal to one. v4 pretrains on distribution and potential fields, freezes the backbone, and trains only the flux head with L1 loss for another 200 epochs. This changes which parameters receive flux supervision, although Section 3 retains its joint-multitask account.

E1.justification: The GKW simulation collection, ion-temperature-gradient turbulence domain, adiabatic-electron approximation and ID/OOD prediction tasks are retained. The new nested training subsets vary data quantity within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain QL, GPR, MLP, FNO, PointNet, Transolver and ViT, alongside the existing factorized CNN/FNO timing comparisons. The saturation-rule comparison also retains the same methods. Newly introduced GyroSwin sizes are configurations of the proposed model.

E3.justification: v4 adds fixed-500-epoch scaling experiments across four pretrained model sizes and nested subsets of 37–241 trajectories. Appendix D also changes the reported binormal representation from real-space y to Fourier-space ky and describes a separate 200-epoch flux-training stage. The training-pair total changes from 44,585 to 44,400. These establish reported protocol revisions, without identifying which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3 replaces fixed-data learning curves with a substantial model/data-size sensitivity analysis, including joint power-law fits and examination of how scaling effects depend on the other axis. Existing component ablations, diagnostic case studies and the linear-simulation saturation-rule experiment remain; the full-model component-ablation results are revised.

E5.justification: v4 adds scaling-specific seed counts, confidence intervals for the joint scaling exponents and a reported seed-to-seed spread. Appendix E specifies two seeds for model-axis points and Medium data-axis runs, and one for XS data-axis runs. The earlier three-seed GyroSwinLinear experiment remains unchanged; no general increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the 48-simulation GyroSwin ID correlation/RMSE pair 26.50/67.68 with 17.67/47.35. Small and Medium results and the final ablation row also change; Large and comparator scores remain unchanged. Small now has the lowest reported 241-simulation flux RMSE, 16.37 ID and 16.73 OOD. Figure 3 adds joint scaling exponents 0.46 and 0.37 while removing the earlier learning curves. Revised training descriptions prevent treating these as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 5 introduces the explicit empirical scaling model L(N,D) = E + A N^(-alpha) + B D^(-beta), a limited mathematical-model addition. The gyrokinetic derivation, quasilinear equations and attention-complexity argument remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable 5D surrogacy, latent integration, mode separation, physical diagnostics, speed and promising scaling. The new quantitative scaling evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the general observation that larger models keep improving with an interpretation that model capacity and data quantity must scale together. It also discusses the unidentifiable irreducible-loss term and differing saturation behavior. Existing interpretations of physical diagnostics and limitations concerning chaos, rollout error and simulation fidelity remain.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E substantially expand reproducibility information through patch/window shapes, layer configurations, conditioning, initialization, normalization, optimizer settings, batch size, checkpoint selection and configuration/FLOP tables. The hardware account changes from H100 setups to 128 GH200 GPUs, while the earlier wall-time estimates are removed. Code and data access links are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to He et al. for initialization, Hendrycks and Gimpel for GELU, and Hoffmann et al. for compute-optimal scaling. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against gyrokinetic reduced models and neural surrogates remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix D is rewritten into labeled implementation topics, bullets and tables, and a new Scaling Configurations appendix shifts subsequent appendix labels. The scalability discussion is rewritten, but the main narrative, section order and most surrounding prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redesigned from epoch-based learning curves into model/data scaling plots with new axes, legends and fitted curves. Three configuration tables are added, Figure 4 is relocated, and the existing ablation and saturation-rule tables are renumbered. Other figures and the overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 adds substantial implementation detail and quantitative scaling evidence with uncertainty estimates. However, its frozen-backbone flux stage is not reconciled with the retained joint-training account, and revised Tables 2 and 7 weaken unchanged generalizations about larger-model and component benefits. These issues affect interpretation of central results, so the documentation gains and consistency problems do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
